paper.title: Stochastic Multi-Objective Multi-Armed Bandits: Regret Definition and Algorithm

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic multi-objective multi-armed bandits (MO-MAB) with coverage / cumulative adjustment regret
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards with Pareto-based regret notions.
unmapped: D-dimensional vector rewards; regret measured against Pareto-optimal (or efficient Pareto-optimal) arms in all objectives simultaneously (coverage-regret and cumulative adjustment-regret)
learner may pull a set of arms A^t per round in the exploitation phase
settings.definition_quote: Given an instance of a MO-MAB problem with \( n \) arms, denoted by \(\mathcal{A}=\{a_1,a_2,...,a_n \}\), and $D$ (maximization) objectives ... In the stochastic setting of the problem \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{r}^t(a) = (T \mu_{1}(a), ..., T\mu_{D}(a))

algorithms.name: A Simple MO-MAB Algorithm (exact minimum set cover)
A Simple MO-MAB Algorithm with O(log n)-approximate set cover
Single arm pulling version of Algorithm 1

conditions: n < T and D < T (used in proof)

source.label: Coverage Theorem
source.quote: The coverage-regret of algorithm \ref{SMOMABA} is \(R = O\left( T^\frac{2}{3} (n\log T)^\frac{1}{3}\right)\).

results.notes: Coverage-regret: for every PO arm a*, max over objectives of T mu_d(a*) - E[sum r_d(a^t)] for a constructed sequence. Proof gives 4T^{2/3}(2n log T)^{1/3} + 2. Theorem 4 states it also holds for EPO arms. Reward range not explicitly stated (Hoeffding used); bounded_01 assumed.

source.label: cumulative adjustment-regret Theorem
source.quote: The cumulative adjustment-regret is hold for algorithm \ref{SMOMABA} with the regret \(R = O\left( T^\frac{2}{3} (n\log T)^\frac{1}{3}\right)\).

results.notes: Cumulative adjustment-regret is bounded by |A*| R. Theorem 4 extends to EPO arms.

source.label: cumulative adjustment-regret Theorem
source.quote: we note that the polynomial-time approximation for the minimum covering set satisfies $|B| \leq \log n \cdot |\mathcal{A}^*|$. Consequently, the polynomial-time algorithm achieves the regret bound of $O\left( \log n \cdot T^{\frac{2}{3}} (n \log T)^{\frac{1}{3}} \right)$ while maintaining correctness.

results.notes: Remark inside the proof of Theorem 3; R = O(log n T^{2/3}(n log T)^{1/3}) so cumulative adjustment-regret is |A*| times that.

source.label: Theorem b_star
source.quote: The regret of the single arm pulling version of Algorithm \ref{SMOMABA} compared to the average best arm $b^*$ is \(R = O\left( T^\frac{2}{3} (n\log T)^\frac{1}{3}\right)\).

results.notes: Regret against a virtual arm b* equal to the mean of a maximal diverse set of PO arms with radius r; nonstandard comparator.
